newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe, S.Africa sign agriculture trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe, S.Africa sign agriculture trade pact.

text.p: Zimbabwe and South Africa signed a trade pact on some agricultural products on Tuesday, moving a step towards a long-awaited comprehensive trade agreement.

The agreement, outlining a quota of Zimbabwean products liable free entry into South Africa and setting out lower import tariffs, was signed by Zimbabwe's Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira and South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin.

The products include beef, cereals, dairy products and poultry, whose exports Zimbabwe officials charge had been badly hit by South Africa's tripling of import duty on a number of products when its preferential trade agreement with neighbouring Zimbabwe expired in 1992.
Since then the two countries have been trying to reach a new comprehensive agreement, and officials say the easy way out is to handle talks sector by sector before putting it all on one paper.

Under the agricultural products agreement signed on Tuesday, Zimbabwe will be able to export up to 5,000 tonnes of beef and 1,000 tonnes of poultry meat duty free, and be liable to pay export duty of around 30 percent for quotas above these levels.
